docs.D00_original_thesis.md:
Title: Late-2021 underwriting — the KCS network combination
Source: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/03/29140526/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2021-Annual-Report.pdf
Date: 2022-03-29

Pershing's March 29, 2022 report states: “Beginning in late 2021, we reinitiated an investment in Canadian Pacific.” This is a distinct investment from the 2011 activist campaign, which ended in 2016. Historical management change supplies background, but the new thesis centers on acquiring and integrating Kansas City Southern.

The letter describes the KCS purchase as “a transformational and value-creating transaction.” The combined network would be the only North American railroad with a direct Canada-to-Mexico route, connect six of the seven largest North American metropolitan regions, and create revenue and cost synergies. At the letter date, CP owned KCS economically through a voting trust but lacked operating control pending regulatory approval.

The business-quality argument was explicit: “We believe CP is an attractive business as it operates in an oligopolistic industry where the barriers to entry are high due to considerable capital requirements, regulation, and network effects.” Rail is often the cheapest or only practical way to move heavy freight over long distances. That mission-critical role supports pricing, but does not make volume immune to economic conditions.

Management execution mattered. The letter says Keith Creel and predecessor Hunter Harrison had more than doubled operating margins from 19% in 2011 to 42% in 2021. It expected CP's leadership to improve KCS operations, while rail's lower long-distance cost and lower emissions could support share gains from trucking.

Valuation was also part of the original case. Despite stronger prospective growth from the combination, shares were described as trading below their historical and peer valuation levels. Successful consummation and integration were expected to produce robust medium-term FCF-per-share growth and a higher valuation more consistent with history and peers.

The essential underwriting tests are therefore merger approval and integration, incremental traffic and synergies, operating discipline, cash generation after necessary rail investment, and the price paid for that growth. Nearshoring and greater North American economic integration were favorable demand assumptions, not guarantees.

This letter does not give a verified original average cost, exact initial PSH cost weight or a precise target price. Those missing figures should not be reconstructed using the much earlier activist position. A current review should compare today's network and policy environment with this specific 2021–22 thesis.
docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: A scarce trilateral rail network with real capital requirements
Source: compiled from: https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/CPKC-2024-Annual-Report-Web_Final.pdf; https://www.cpkcr.com/en/media/Q4-2024-Results
Date: 2025-02-25

Canadian Pacific Kansas City provides freight rail transportation across Canada, the United States and Mexico. Its network combines legacy Canadian Pacific with Kansas City Southern, operating under common control since April 14, 2023. The single-line service proposition reduces interchange complexity for some cross-border routes and creates new customer options.

Rail has physical network advantages. Building competing rights of way, track, terminals and operating capacity is expensive, time-consuming and heavily regulated. Existing route density and connections matter. These barriers support an oligopolistic industry structure, but competition remains from other railroads, trucking, water transport and alternative routing.

Customers move commodities and industrial products as well as intermodal freight. Demand depends on agricultural production, energy and industrial activity, trade patterns and consumer supply chains. Some traffic is essential, yet annual tonnage and mix remain cyclical. Price increases can partly offset inflation without fully offsetting a major volume shock.

FY2024 freight revenue was C$14.223 billion and non-freight revenue C$323 million, for total revenue C$14.546 billion. Operating income was C$5.179 billion. The reported 64.4% operating ratio means operating expense divided by revenue; lower is better. It is not EBITDA margin, and depreciation is included in operating expense.

Keith Creel is president and CEO. The thesis relies on operating execution, safe and reliable service, network capacity and realization of merger synergies. Procurement efficiencies and better asset utilization can improve margins; revenue synergies require customers to adopt new services and depend partly on trade flows.

This is not a capital-light platform. FY2024 additions to properties were C$2.825 billion, plus C$38 million to Meridian Speedway properties. Long-lived infrastructure requires continuing maintenance and investment. Accounting earnings, EBITDA and spendable FCF are consequently different economic measures.

Year-end debt was C$22.623 billion including current maturities, against C$739 million cash. The company had 933.5 million common shares outstanding. Debt was part of financing the combined network, making deleveraging and cash discipline relevant even when the operating franchise remains strong.

The key business-quality distinction is between scarcity of the network and variability of the freight moving over it. Tariffs can affect traffic, customer investment and routing without eliminating rights-of-way advantages. A durable network is necessary but not sufficient for a predictable short-to-medium-term earnings path.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Three annual statements — consolidation changes the comparison
Source: https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/CPKC-2024-Annual-Report-Web_Final.pdf
Date: 2025-02-25

All dollar amounts are C$ millions except per-share figures. These are audited reported statements, not a pro forma combined-company growth series. Before April 14, 2023, KCS was equity-accounted; thereafter it was consolidated. The 2022–24 revenue growth implied by the table is therefore not organic growth.

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 8,814 | 12,555 | 14,546 |
| Operating income | 3,329 | 4,388 | 5,179 |
| Calculated operating margin | 37.8% | 34.9% | 35.6% |
| Diluted EPS | 3.77 | 4.21 | 3.98 |
| Operating cash flow | 4,142 | 4,137 | 5,269 |
| Additions to properties | 1,557 | 2,468 | 2,825 |
| Meridian property additions | — | 31 | 38 |
| CFO less both property lines, calculated | 2,585 | 1,638 | 2,406 |
| Cash dividends | 707 | 707 | 709 |
| Year-end cash | 451 | 464 | 739 |

The calculated cash residual is a transparent CFO-minus-investment measure, not the company's defined adjusted FCF. It excludes proceeds from asset sales and other investing adjustments. FY2024 property-sale proceeds were C$64 million. Exact comparability to management's free-cash-flow presentation requires its reconciliation.

FY2023 net income contains a C$7.175 billion KCS remeasurement loss and C$7.885 billion deferred-tax recovery. These offsetting acquisition-accounting effects make GAAP EPS growth a poor stand-alone indicator of recurring operations. FY2024 reported EPS fell while the January earnings release reports 11% core adjusted combined EPS growth.

At December 31, 2024, current debt maturities were C$2.819 billion and long-term debt C$19.804 billion, total C$22.623 billion. Less C$739 million cash gives calculated net debt C$21.884 billion, before any further lease or pension adjustment. The 2023 corresponding debt sum was C$22.494 billion and cash C$464 million.

Common shares outstanding were 933.5 million versus 932.1 million. FY2024 diluted weighted-average shares were 934.6 million. No cash-flow repurchase line appears in this table; forecast repurchases should not be presented as already executed.

Latest Q4 reported revenue was approximately C$3.9 billion, reported EPS C$1.28 and core adjusted combined EPS C$1.29. Full-year core adjusted combined EPS was C$4.25. A harmonized adjusted EBITDA or ROIC series has not been extracted, so neither is manufactured from mixed accounting bases.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: January results and the public 2025 growth case
Source: compiled from: https://www.cpkcr.com/en/media/Q4-2024-Results; https://financialpost.com/transportation/rail/tariff-threat-cpkc-forcasts-trade-growth; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf
Date: 2025-03-14

CPKC's January 29 release reports Q4 revenue of approximately C$3.9 billion, up 3% from C$3.8 billion. Reported EPS was C$1.28 and core adjusted combined EPS C$1.29. The reported operating ratio was 59.7%; the core adjusted combined ratio was 57.1%. These are different bases, not interchangeable precision alternatives.

Christopher Reynolds of Canadian Press, writing January 29 and updated January 30 in Financial Post, reports adjusted EPS above the C$1.24 analyst expectation. Management's constructive tone therefore followed actual operational outperformance rather than only a distant merger promise.

The January guidance calls for core adjusted diluted EPS growth of 12–18% from 2024's C$4.25. Calculated, that implies C$4.76–5.015 per share. Management expects mid-single-digit revenue-ton-mile growth and C$2.9 billion capital spending. The release notes a higher USD/CAD rate contributes to the capex increase.

Creel says, “I think a pragmatic approach will carry the day,” in response to the tariff threat, per the Canadian Press report. His view is that integrated North American supply chains will continue to require rail service. This is a management judgment about policy and customer behavior, not a binding assurance from the US administration.

Pershing's March 14 annual report supplies an independently public thesis update. It reports more than $800 million of run-rate revenue synergies, exceeding management expectations, plus operational/procurement savings. The paragraph's dollar denomination is not repeated explicitly, so this pack does not relabel that figure as USD or CAD.

The report says these synergies supported 11% EPS growth in 2024 despite labor disruptions and a difficult freight market. It argues that both predecessor businesses grew EPS at mid-teens annual rates during the first Trump administration. That historical analogy supports resilience but does not prove the current tariff regime will have identical effects.

The last recovered company guidance remains the January range. No April results, later revision or eventual realized 2025 effect belongs in this March snapshot. The immediate tension is between demonstrated synergy execution and a policy environment that may change cross-border volumes more quickly than the railway can adjust fixed costs.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: March 17 valuation in matched currencies
Source: compiled from: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CP.TO/history/?period1=1742169600&period2=1742256000; https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CP/history/?period1=1742169600&period2=1742256000; https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/CPKC-2024-Annual-Report-Web_Final.pdf; https://www.cpkcr.com/en/media/Q4-2024-Results
Date: 2025-03-17

Toronto-listed CP closed March 17 at C$107.54, with 1,037,900 shares traded, an open of C$107.82 and daily range C$106.67–107.95. The matching NYSE close was US$75.29 on 1,956,300 shares, with range US$74.64–75.58. These are unadjusted historical closes, not today's dividend-adjusted series.

The financial statements and EPS are in Canadian dollars. Valuation below therefore uses the Toronto close, rather than dividing a US-dollar price by Canadian-dollar earnings. The simultaneous price ratio is not treated as a separately authenticated FX fixing.

Using year-end 933.5 million shares outstanding, calculated equity value is C$100.390 billion. Adding C$21.884 billion calculated net debt yields EV of C$122.274 billion. These are stale-share/balance-sheet proxies, not exact cutoff capitalization. The March price date is more recent than the December denominator.

| Calculated measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| FY2024 reported P/E, C$3.98 EPS | 27.0x |
| FY2024 core adjusted combined P/E, C$4.25 EPS | 25.3x |
| P/E on 2025 management EPS range | 21.4–22.6x |
| FY2024 CFO-minus-both-property-lines yield | 2.4% |
| EV / FY2024 reported operating income | 23.6x |

The forward ratio uses company guidance, not analyst consensus. It assumes the announced growth range remains achievable. Reported operating income is not EBITDA; the last row must not be mislabeled EV/EBITDA.

The cash yield uses C$2.406 billion from D02, not company-adjusted FCF. Rail spending includes maintenance and growth, and the source does not provide a clean allocation sufficient to treat all capex as discretionary.

An exact cutoff 52-week range, five-to-ten-year historical multiple distribution, consensus forward EPS, peer forward multiples and S&P 500 forward multiple were not authenticated. No unsupported claim that the stock is at a record multiple is made.

The original thesis anticipated some rerating, but the available evidence cannot isolate how much of the current multiple reflects realized synergy benefits, macro optimism or scarcity value. Prospective returns must be evaluated using current earnings uncertainty and current price, not the success of the much earlier activist investment.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Trade-policy uncertainty versus network resilience
Source: compiled from: https://financialpost.com/transportation/rail/tariff-threat-cpkc-forcasts-trade-growth; https://abcnews.com/Business/stocks-tumble-tariff-fallout-roils-markets/story?id=119508907; https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/03/03/trump-tariffs-canada-mexico-tuesday/81172627007; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf
Date: 2025-03-14

The central bear mechanism is that a network built to benefit from North American economic integration is unusually exposed to policy that disrupts that integration. Higher tariffs can reduce trade, delay customer investment, change sourcing and alter the mix of rail shipments. Track scarcity does not protect against every reduction in freight demand.

Bart Jansen's March 3 USA Today account reports President Trump's statement that 25% tariffs on imports from Canada and Mexico would begin the next day. ABC News' Max Zahn, March 6, reports a temporary pause for goods compliant with the USMCA, expanding an automaker carve-out. The exemption is a current policy fact, not proof that the dispute is permanently resolved.

Repeated announcements and temporary relief can create uncertainty even when some immediate shipments are exempt. Customers may postpone orders, build inventory ahead of changes or reroute supply chains. Timing effects could initially make traffic look stronger before weakening, so a single week's carloads would be insufficient evidence of long-term resilience.

The January Canadian Press report captures the bullish counterargument. Creel expects pragmatism because integrated supply chains remain valuable. Pershing's March 14 report similarly emphasizes nearshoring, predecessor earnings growth during the first Trump administration and the necessity of continued regional trade for US growth.

Those statements are explicitly forward-looking. Prior tariffs were not necessarily identical in scope, duration or retaliation. The key analytical question is whether earnings can remain predictable enough under several plausible policy paths, not whether the network has suddenly become unnecessary.

Other risks include fixed-cost operating leverage, fuel and labor costs, service disruptions, integration complexity and substantial capital requirements. FY2024 debt net of cash was approximately C$21.9 billion. Strong free cash generation helps, but debt and required infrastructure spending reduce flexibility if volumes deteriorate sharply.

Counterevidence includes a strong Q4 ratio, adjusted EPS above expectations and already-realized merger revenue synergies. A skeptical case must explain why those gains are insufficient rather than pretend they do not exist.

No dated pre-cutoff source here proves a permanent loss of competitive position. The strongest evidence concerns a wider range of macro outcomes. That uncertainty matters particularly for a concentrated investor whose standard includes limited exposure to uncontrollable extrinsic factors.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: Rail operating benchmarks and different network exposures
Source: compiled from: https://www.cn.ca/-/media/files/investors/investor-annual-report/2024-cn-annual-report.pdf; https://investor.unionpacific.com/news-releases/news-release-details/union-pacific-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results; https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/CPKC-2024-Annual-Report-Web_Final.pdf
Date: 2025-03-14

Canadian National and Union Pacific provide relevant operating comparisons. Both have extensive established networks, significant capital requirements and cyclical freight exposure. Neither exactly replicates CPKC's single-line Canada–US–Mexico service, so the investment case cannot be reduced to choosing the lowest operating ratio.

| FY2024 public metric | CPKC | Canadian National | Union Pacific |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | C$14.546bn | C$17.046bn | Not extracted |
| Reported operating ratio | 64.4% | 63.4% | 59.9% |
| Adjusted operating ratio | Basis differs; not harmonized here | 62.9% | Not separately supplied |
| Reported diluted EPS | C$3.98 | C$7.01 | US$11.09 |
| Operating income | C$5.179bn | C$6.247bn | Not extracted |

Canadian National's report says revenue grew 1%, while operating income fell 5% and reported operating ratio worsened 2.6 percentage points. The adjusted ratio worsened 2.1 points. Industry-wide infrastructure advantages therefore do not guarantee annual margin expansion.

Union Pacific's January 23 release reports FY2024 EPS up 6%, a 59.9% operating ratio and 15.8% return on invested capital. Q4 EPS was $2.91, up 7%, and operating ratio 58.7%. These figures demonstrate a high-quality peer benchmark, but US-dollar EPS and a different business mix prevent direct share-price comparisons.

CPKC's acquisition accounting includes larger depreciation and amortization from combining businesses. Adjusted combined metrics attempt to improve economic comparability, but use of them requires explicit reconciliation rather than selectively pairing adjusted CPKC results with unadjusted peers.

The industry's competitive moat is common: rail corridors are hard to reproduce and efficient for long-distance bulk freight. Differentiation comes from route geography, service reliability, customer mix, pricing, network fluidity and capital allocation. Trucking is also an important alternative, particularly over shorter distances and where customers value flexibility.

Trade-policy exposure differs with geography and freight composition. CPKC's unique trilateral route is both a strategic advantage and a channel through which a cross-border volume shock could matter. A peer with lower direct exposure may still suffer indirectly through industrial demand.

Exact March 17 peer market values, consensus P/E and FCF yields were not verified. The pack supplies operating evidence without presenting a false precise relative-valuation ranking.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: Integration progress meets a changing policy environment
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/03/29140526/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2021-Annual-Report.pdf; https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/CPKC-2024-Annual-Report-Web_Final.pdf; https://www.cpkcr.com/en/media/Q4-2024-Results; https://abcnews.com/Business/stocks-tumble-tariff-fallout-roils-markets/story?id=119508907; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf
Date: 2025-03-17

Late 2021: Pershing reinitiated a CP investment. Its March 2022 explanation focuses on the KCS acquisition, management execution, merger synergies and a valuation below history and peers. This is not the start of the original activist campaign.

December 2021: CP acquired KCS economically through a voting trust. Pending operating-control approval, KCS contributed through equity accounting rather than full consolidation. This distinction later affects the historical financial tables.

April 14, 2023: CPKC obtained control and consolidated KCS. The trilateral network became an operating combination rather than only an anticipated strategic concept. Reported 2023 accounts contain major acquisition-related tax and remeasurement items.

During 2024: Integration synergies progressed despite labor disruptions and a difficult freight market. FY2024 statements show stronger CFO, but ongoing investment and debt remain substantial. Full-year reported EPS and adjusted combined EPS move differently because their accounting bases differ.

January 29, 2025: CPKC reported Q4 adjusted EPS C$1.29 and gave 12–18% core adjusted EPS growth guidance for 2025, with mid-single-digit ton-mile growth and C$2.9 billion capital spending. Management expressed confidence in continued cross-border commerce despite tariff threats.

February 25: The 2024 annual report made full reported financial statements available. It documents C$14.546 billion revenue, C$5.269 billion CFO and C$22.623 billion debt before cash.

March 3–6: US tariff announcements were followed by a temporary exemption for USMCA-compliant Canadian and Mexican goods. Policy remains unsettled rather than definitively hostile to every shipment or definitively resolved.

March 14: Pershing's published annual report reiterated a constructive CPKC thesis, citing realized run-rate revenue synergies, management, regional integration and double-digit prospective earnings/FCF-per-share growth. That public statement is important counterevidence against assuming the thesis was already abandoned.

March 17: Toronto shares closed C$107.54 and NYSE shares US$75.29. This is the review date. Later tariff decisions, quarterly results, portfolio disclosures and price outcomes are excluded. The live question is how much policy uncertainty should alter confidence in the previously articulated growth case.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Public year-end ownership and portfolio opportunity cost
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/07152731/Performance-Report-September-2024-PSH.pdf
Date: 2025-03-14

The March 14 report gives December 31 PSH net assets of approximately $13.01 billion. The latest recovered wider firm AUM is September 30, 2024, $18.4988 billion including PSVII and bond proceeds. This is stale gross AUM, not March NAV or free buying power.

The audited PSH schedule provides actual fund-NAV weights, unlike a US 13F-only table. CPKC was 13,267,340 shares worth $960.157 million, or 7.38% of PSH net assets, at December 31. That is a market-value allocation, not original cost weight and not current March exposure.

Other disclosed year-end weights included Universal Music 23.11%, Alphabet A/C together 15.12%, Chipotle 10.19%, Nike 9.86%, Howard Hughes 9.77% and Hilton 9.21%. The listed common-stock total exceeded 100% of NAV because gross exposure is financed partly by fund-level debt. These weights should not be forced to sum to 100% by omitting financing or other assets.

Cash and equivalents were approximately $436.5 million at year-end. Liquidity, other instruments and financing mean this is not all deployable firm capital. The March report also publicly discusses Uber as a new investment; no future transaction is inferred from that fact.

Pershing's published CPKC commentary remains constructive. It describes a “high-quality, inflation-protected North American railroad” and a “best-in-class management team.” It expects double-digit earnings and FCF-per-share growth supported by synergies, pricing and repurchases. Tariff uncertainty is acknowledged but countered with regional economic integration and predecessor resilience.

This context matters because the decision is not between owning a railroad and holding nothing forever. A concentrated fund compares each position's prospective return and forecastability with available alternatives. Strong historical management execution and a scarce network must be weighed against current policy sensitivity and the capital required to support that network.

The report's preferences for durable competitive advantages, predictable cash generation, sound balance sheets and capable management are relevant. They do not predetermine a current decision. No later portfolio action or post-March public macro commentary is part of this document.

Exact March weights, a full recent-exit register and the complete firm cash position remain unavailable. The dated year-end PSH schedule is the honest ownership baseline.
docs.D09_what_has_changed.md:
Title: Testing the 2021 KCS thesis at the March 2025 checkpoint
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2022/03/29140526/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2021-Annual-Report.pdf; https://s21.q4cdn.com/736796105/files/doc_financials/2024/ar/CPKC-2024-Annual-Report-Web_Final.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/03/14183709/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2024-Annual-Report-1.pdf; https://abcnews.com/Business/stocks-tumble-tariff-fallout-roils-markets/story?id=119508907
Date: 2025-03-14

The initial investment anticipated obtaining operating control, realizing synergies, improving KCS operations and compounding FCF per share. Several risks have diminished. Regulatory uncertainty over obtaining control is no longer the central live issue: the combination has operated under common control since April 2023.

Synergies are no longer only a presentation forecast. The March 14 Pershing report cites more than $800 million run-rate revenue synergies and ongoing cost savings. FY2024 CFO rose to C$5.269 billion from C$4.137 billion, while adjusted combined EPS grew 11%. These observations support important parts of the original underwriting.

The quality of the network and management has not visibly disappeared. The same published report praises the trilateral route, management execution and long-term cash generation. An assessment claiming established competitive deterioration would need evidence beyond the material included here.

What has changed is the policy backdrop. Nearshoring and increasing North American integration were favorable original assumptions. Broad tariffs, retaliation and repeated temporary exemptions create a wider range of possible traffic and customer-investment paths. The unique network's greatest strategic differentiator is consequently also a source of direct policy sensitivity.

There is an important counterargument: integrated supply chains are costly to rebuild, USMCA-compliant shipments have temporary relief, and management still guides to double-digit EPS growth. The prior administration's tariff experience offers some resilience evidence. None of that makes current policy decisions controllable by the railway.

Financial flexibility remains a separate test. The combined company has C$22.623 billion debt before cash and plans C$2.9 billion 2025 capex. Its required infrastructure spending means EBITDA cannot be treated as fully distributable cash. Volume shocks would affect a fixed-cost business while maintenance needs continue.

The stock trades at about 25.3x FY2024 adjusted combined EPS and 21.4–22.6x the company's 2025 guided range. Exact rerating since entry is not established because original average cost and consistent historical multiples were not recovered.

The current decision therefore requires distinguishing successful integration from changing forward risk. It is possible for the operational thesis to be progressing while prospective risk-adjusted attractiveness changes. It is equally possible for policy noise to leave long-term economics largely intact. The evidence does not justify replacing either possibility with hindsight.

Management guidance for 12-18% adjusted EPS growth in 2025 provides a clear path to double-digit returns, supported by realized operational improvements [D04].

final.memo:
Our investment in the Company remains a conviction position as the operational thesis has played out successfully since we reinitiated our investment in late 2021 [D00, D08]. The Company has achieved the critical milestone of operating control over the combined trilateral network, and the integration is delivering tangible value, with over $800 million in run-rate revenue synergies realized [D04, D08, D10]. These operational gains supported 11% EPS growth in 2024 despite a challenging freight environment, demonstrating the resilience of our thesis [D04].

We acknowledge the current policy backdrop is more complex than originally assumed. The emergence of potential tariffs on cross-border trade introduces extrinsic factors that we cannot control [D06, D10]. However, we agree with management’s assessment that the North American supply chain is structurally dependent on rail, and the precedent of the first Trump administration suggests that the Company is well-positioned to maintain mid-teens EPS growth even in periods of trade policy flux [D04, D06]. The temporary exemptions for USMCA-compliant goods further mitigate the immediate threat to the network's volume predictability [D06, D08].

With the stock trading at approximately 21.4–22.6x our 2025 earnings estimate, we are paying a fair price for a high-quality, free-cash-flow-generative business with durable growth prospects [D05, D09]. The Company's capital requirements are substantial, but its strong cash generation and disciplined management give us confidence in its ability to navigate cyclical and policy-driven headwinds [D02, D10]. Given the strength of the underlying franchise and the management team’s proven execution, we continue to hold our position with high conviction [D09, D10].

drivers.driver: The core investment thesis is progressing, evidenced by successful network integration, synergy realization, and double-digit management guidance for 2025 EPS growth [D04, D08].

final.memo:
Our investment in Canadian Pacific Kansas City remains a cornerstone of the portfolio because the fundamental business quality we underwrote—a scarce, trilateral rail network with high barriers to entry and best-in-class management—has been proven through the successful integration of Kansas City Southern [D02, D08]. Since the merger attained common control in April 2023, management has demonstrably executed on its plan, delivering over $800 million in run-rate revenue synergies and robust operational discipline [D04, D08]. 

We acknowledge the current policy environment introduces noise regarding cross-border trade, but we view the necessity of integrated North American supply chains as a strong buffer [D06, D10]. The management team’s 2025 guidance of 12–18% core adjusted EPS growth, supported by underlying demand for rail, aligns with our expectation for durable, long-term compounding [D04].
